episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. We not only cover football & basketball, but we dive into recruiting, baseball, soccer, and more. For insight that you can't get anywhere else, tune into 103.9/ 98.3 FM. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.

transcript_window.text: kick on ABC.
So we got a great time slot that opening weekend.
And ultimately what we're trying to do with this game is kick off the season in Atlanta.
Atlanta, we unabashedly feel like Atlanta is the capital of college football.
So putting a game like this in Mercedes -Benz Stadium, right in the middle of the heart of the South, it's a great way to kick off the game.
And Atlanta is such a town that's built around college football and college sports that the city mobilizes behind it.
Whether it's Baylor or Auburn or whether it would be bringing in a Clemson or a Georgia or an Arizona State, the city just loves college football.

So doing it on that stage gives us a chance to, one, distinguish ourselves in the city, but also just to bring college football back into the market in a place that's not necessarily Georgia or Georgia Tech or one of the teams that everybody always sees.
The last five years, you look at Virginia Tech versus South Carolina, Syracuse, Tennessee, Clemson, Georgia.
That was a nice one.
As far as ranking was concerned, it was a dominant victory for Georgia.
Louisville, Georgia Tech, Clemson, Georgia Tech, Oregon, Georgia, Louisville, Ole Miss, Alabama versus Miami.
So when you guys are strategizing here in your executive meetings, right, and you're trying to find the right teams to match up, give us that process.
What does this look like to execute a kickoff games between two powerful institutions?
Yeah, it's a really fascinating process, and it's changed a lot.
Just the way the college football has changed in the in the CFP expansion era, I would say.
I mean, even when we were four teams, it changed a little bit.
But when it was four teams and you could play a game against a big opponent during week one of the season.
The win there obviously propelled you in the rankings.

rankings a loss didn't necessarily sink you because you had the rest of the season to claw your way back into the conversation in moving into the 12 team playoff it changed the the stakes a little bit because the coaches now start questioning what is the cfp committee valuing yeah you know this happened last year where you're saying all
right a texas for example you know they played that game against ohio state we got around to december everybody's questioning whether texas should make it in or not.

If Texas had not played Ohio State and they had played, you know, I'm not going to name a team, but somebody who was a guaranteed win, all of a sudden their 10 -win team going into December, people aren't discussing that as much.
So I think the big question now for us is we've got to find teams and coaches that have availability on their schedules.
You have to find a coach that's willing to take on an opponent that could potentially harm their resume as they're going through the rest of the season.
And the added wrinkle in all this is that with all the conferences going to nine conference games, you know, you look at a 12 game schedule.
If you've got nine and then let's say you have a rivalry game outside of that, you know, 10 of your games are already locked down.
